headline: Your 10:30 is TODAY, not tomorrow — an HVAC contractor walks your Lake Crest seller's house in under three hours and he still has not been told, while at 355 Comanche the buyers countered back at 7:59 last night and you promised their agent an answer this morning.

hotSignals.signal: 🔴 THE CLOCK MOVED FROM TOMORROW TO THIS MORNING. The second inspection on this file lands 10:30–11:30 TODAY, booked Sunday at 3:18 PM by buyer's agent Manda L. (ARC Realty Vestavia), and the showing remark reads verbatim: "Meeting hvac company." Friday's repair request has still never arrived, so this remains the only hard signal of what the buyers are actually chasing. Two more receipts sharpen it: the 7/24 certificate-of-completion visit NEVER HAPPENED — the inspector left without conducting it — and Gene's own question to his coordinator about the city's final permit has been sitting as an UNSENT draft since Saturday 10:44 AM. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED: that anything is wrong with the HVAC, what a contractor will find, what it would cost, or that any of this threatens the close. The receipt says an HVAC company is being met, nothing more.
hotSignals.action: Call your seller before 10:30 so he is not surprised by strangers at his house — and do NOT open by announcing a problem you cannot name. Same call, get the thing that has now been asked five times: a weekday DATE the sellers meet the city, not "next week." Send the coordinator draft that has been sitting since Saturday; it is the cheapest item on this file. Then give Manda L. the date — she texted on a Saturday citing a clock, and a real date is what turns worry into a timeline. Don't re-litigate whether the buyers should be concerned. Then the free move nobody has made: the written "interested: Yes" backup buyer, Kulsum B. (Keller Williams Hoover), is eight days uncalled — and she is the same agent booked on Ridge Trail, so one call does both.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE BUYERS CAME BACK — AND THEY BLEW PAST THEIR OWN DEADLINE TO DO IT. Buyer's agent Cassie C. (RE/MAX Advantage) texted at 7:59 PM Sunday: "Please forgive my text, I'm at dinner and it's very loud here. I just heard back from my buyers. They'd like to counter back…" — 59 minutes AFTER the expiry her own written offer had set. Read the behaviour ahead of the number: a side that lets its own deadline lapse and then answers from a restaurant table is buying, not walking. The full trail is receipted: Saturday's feedback ("interested: Yes" · priced "Too high" · "Writing up an offer!"), the written offer four minutes later, Gene's net sheet and counter recommendation SENT to his seller Sunday 9:50 AM, the seller's 11:43 reply from a boat, Cassie's 3:01 PM "Any news?", Gene's 3:17 PM "counter sent" text and the 👍🏻 back — then the counter-counter at 7:59 PM. Verified on three independent sources.
hotSignals.action: You already texted her at 5:41 this morning: "will get you a response this am." That promise is now the clock on this file — do not let noon arrive without her hearing something. Order of operations: seller first (he answers fast — boat reply in under two hours, thumbs-up in one minute), then Cassie. The decision in front of you is small: hold, or split the remaining gap. The spread is narrow enough that certainty may be worth more than the last few thousand — but that is your call and your seller's. ⚠️ Their pre-approval is papered BELOW their own counter, so either way their lender likely has to re-paper; build a day or two in rather than reading a pause as a problem. ⚠️ And the genuinely open question since 7/16 is unchanged: is the ARC Realty offer alive? If it is, your seller is CHOOSING between two offers rather than waiting on one, and you can hold much harder. Confirm before he answers.

hotSignals.signal: ⭐ THE THING THAT HAS BLOCKED THIS RE-OFFER FOR TWO WEEKS MOVES TODAY. The buyers behind Kenneth R.'s conditional re-offer are listing their own Sterrett house TODAY (his SMS, Sunday 5:16 PM) — that house not being under contract is the entire reason the re-offer has had no legs. Separately, Sunday's 3:00 showing (Quin W., EXIT Realty Southern Select, showing #11) cancelled at 11:44 AM because the buyer got called into work — a scheduling problem, not a lost buyer, so the third distinct buyer in eight days is still live.
hotSignals.action: Two moves, in order. Rebook with Quin W. FIRST so you reach your seller with a date instead of an apology — he occupies this house and has heard nothing from you in eight days, re-verified across email, sent mail and SMS. Then use today's real lever with Kenneth R.: their house going live is the day to ask for movement, because until it is under contract the re-offer is a wish. The 96-hour bar passed Sunday with the same answer as the 48- and 72-hour bars. ✅ A feedback nudge on the 7/23 showing finally went out at 7:12 this morning — watch for William K.'s read.

(Counts Real Estate Group) at 7:13 this morning, closing a gap that had been open three days on the first activity this unit has seen in weeks. She showed it Saturday 9:30 AM at 126 days on market, ending the longest zero-activity streak on the board, and she left a note in the app — so there is genuinely something to collect here.

Feedback on this listing has NEVER come back unprompted and the last read (7/1) was "not interested," so asking is the whole game. Frame the market context for him so the call isn't about his unit: PCB ran 68 sold against 218 new listings in mid-July. ⚠️ Still no email on file for him — capture it on the call.
